steps.message:
The build succeeds and the fix is in place.

## Diagnosis

**File:** `app/src/main/java/com/trianguloy/urlchecker/modules/list/UriPartsModule.java`

The module parsed query parameters with `UrlQuerySanitizer` fed from `uri.getQuery()`:

```java
urlQuerySanitizer.parseQuery(uri.getQuery().replace("%", "%25"));
```

`Uri.getQuery()` returns the **already percent-decoded** query. So for `https://example.com/?q=a%26b%3Dc` it returns `q=a&b=c`. The sanitizer then split that decoded string on `&` and `=`, so the encoded separators were mistaken for real ones → two parameters (`q → a`, `b → c`) instead of one (`q → a&b=c`).

The `.replace("%", "%25")` hack was a workaround for the resulting double-decoding, but it can't help: by the time it runs, the separators have already been turned into literal `&`/`=`.

## Fix

Split the query while it is **still encoded** (`uri.getEncodedQuery()`), then decode each name/value exactly once:

- Added `splitQueryParameters(String encodedQuery)` — splits the raw query on `&`, then on the first `=`, keeping the encoded pair, name and value (small `QueryParameter` holder class).
- Names/values are decoded with the existing `UrlUtils.decode` (`URLDecoder`), which decodes exactly once, handles multi-byte UTF-8 correctly (`%C3%A9 → é` — the old `UrlQuerySanitizer.unescape` decoded byte-per-char and mangled these), and falls back to the raw string on malformed escapes like `%zz`.
- The per-parameter delete button now rebuilds the query from the **original encoded** pairs via `encodedQuery(...)`, so removing one parameter no longer re-encodes (and potentially alters) the others; `null` is used when nothing is left so the `?` is dropped.
- Dropped the now-unused `android.net.UrlQuerySanitizer` import.

Verified behavior with a standalone harness of the same logic:

| URL | Result |
|---|---|
| `?q=a%26b%3Dc` | `q → a&b=c` ✅ (was `q → a`, `b → c`) |
| `?q=a&b=c` | `q → a`, `b → c` (unchanged) |
| `?q=caf%C3%A9&x=100%25` | `q → café`, `x → 100%` |
| `?url=https%3A%2F%2Fo.com%2F%3Fa%3D1%26b%3D2&ref=x#frag` | `url → https://o.com/?a=1&b=2`, `ref → x`; deleting `ref` yields `?url=https%3A%2F%2Fo.com%2F%3Fa%3D1%26b%3D2#frag` |

`./gradlew clean assembleDebug` → **BUILD SUCCESSFUL**.
